title: Reading Between The Lines: Modeling and Evaluating Behavioral Realism in Legal Simulation
abstract: arXiv:2608.13712v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Deposition training requires attorneys to manage dynamic witness behavior, yet legal-AI evaluations largely focus on factual accuracy, reasoning, or response-level plausibility. We introduce WitnessSim, a deposition simulator driven by controllable legal personas. We use an evaluation framework separating behavioral realism from pedagogical usefulness. We assess realism through adversarial testing, blinded attorney comparison, and analysis of longitudinal behavioral trajectories. WitnessSim generally maintained plausible behavioral boundaries, and attorneys did not systematically prefer either original testimony or WitnessSim generated testimony. Pedagogical tests showed that witness behavior changed meaningfully in response to question form and attorney intervention without uniformly collapsing the assigned persona. translated_title: 字里行间：法律模拟中行为真实性的建模与评估
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.13712v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：证词培训要求律师管理动态的证人行为，然而法律人工智能的评估主要侧重于事实准确性、推理或回应层面的合理性。我们引入了WitnessSim，一种由可控法律人格驱动的证词模拟器。我们使用一种将行为真实性与教学实用性分离的评估框架。我们通过对抗性测试、盲审律师比较以及纵向行为轨迹分析来评估真实性。WitnessSim通常能维持合理的行为边界，律师并未系统性地偏好原始证词或WitnessSim生成的证词。教学测试表明，证人行为会随着问题形式和律师干预而有意义地变化，而不会统一瓦解所指定的人格。综合这些结果，我们展示了一种法律模拟中行为保真度的模型，并为评估提供了框架。
tldr: 本文提出WitnessSim模拟器，通过分离行为真实性与教学实用性，验证了可控法律人格在证词模拟中能保持行为边界并响应交互，为法律AI评估提供了新框架。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces WitnessSim, a deposition simulator with controllable legal personas, and demonstrates through a separated evaluation framework that it maintains behavioral realism and responds to interactions, offering a new paradigm for legal-AI assessment.
